nodes.description: Asymmetric electrolyzer performance at 25°C (flow cell 4.0 cm²)
nodes.source_text: Pt/C and IrO₂ paired catalysts at 25°C exhibit a current density of 0.1 A cm⁻² at cell voltage of 5.0 V. This current density is exhibited at 2.5 V via replacing IrO₂ to NiFe-LDH. The cell voltage decreases to 1.8 V with Pt/WO₂ as the cathode. Significantly, just 3.0 V is required to exhibit 0.5 A cm⁻² at 25°C
A similar performance for the catalysts was exhibited in simulated seawater, viz., 0.6 M NaCl without Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ and the pH was controlled to 8.3 via addition of KOH (1.0 M)

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure monoclinic phase of WO₂ (PDF no. 32-1393) and presence of Pt species (PDF no. 87-0640) confirmed for Pt/WO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) findings confirmed a pure monoclinic phase of WO₂ (PDF no. 32-1393) and the presence of Pt species (PDF no. 87-0640, Figure 1a, Figure S1, and Table S1).

properties.description: Experimental XRD pattern of Pt/WO2 sample

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt nanoparticles ca. 5 nm in size loaded on WO₂ skeleton with lattice parameter of 0.345 nm for WO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images showed that Pt nanoparticles ca. 5 nm in size are loaded on the WO₂ skeleton with a lattice parameter of 0.345 nm for WO₂ (Figure 1b and Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electronic interaction between Pt and WO₂ makes vibrational peak for Pt/WO₂ weaker compared with pure WO₂, establishing Pt nanoparticles anchored on WO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Raman spectroscopy (Figure 1c), the electronic interaction between Pt and WO₂ makes the vibrational peak for Pt/WO₂ weaker compared with pure WO₂, establishing that Pt nanoparticles are anchored on WO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS Pt 4f confirms Pt⁰ states in Pt/WO₂ with Pt in Ptᵟ⁻ states vs Pt/C (Ptᵟ⁺ states); greater binding energy for lattice oxygen and W⁴⁺ 4f states in Pt/WO₂ vs WO₂ confirms electron migration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) findings confirmed that Pt⁰ states existed in Pt/WO₂ (Figure 1d). Notably, Pt in the Pt/WO₂ catalyst were in Ptᵟ⁻ states, in contrast to standard Pt/C (Ptᵟ⁺ states). Additionally, compared with WO₂ a greater binding energy for the lattice oxygen and W⁴⁺ 4f states for Pt/WO₂ confirmed this migration (Figure S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt, W, and O homogeneously dispersed throughout nanoparticle-like Pt/WO₂ cluster.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping analysis confirmed that Pt, W, and O were homogeneously dispersed throughout the nanoparticle-like Pt/WO₂ cluster (Figures S2 and S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/WO₂ exhibits significantly greater absorbance than WO₂ due to more oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: More oxygen vacancies (O_Vs) in Pt/WO₂ were readily identifiable than that for WO₂ (Figure S6b); therefore, it exhibited significantly greater absorbance than that for WO₂ (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Two peaks at 350 and 554 nm boosted with cathodal potential, evidencing more oxygen vacancies generated during electrocatalysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ ultraviolet-visible UV-vis absorption spectroscopy confirmed two peaks at 350 and 554 nm boosted with the cathodal potential, evidencing that more oxygen vacancies generated during electrocatalysis favor charge storage (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge XANES confirms presence of Ptᵟ⁻ states in Pt/WO₂, reflected in slightly lower intensity of white-line peak than Pt foil.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S5, Pt L₃-edge X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES) for catalysts further confirmed the presence of Ptᵟ⁻ states, which was reflected in the slightly lower intensity of the white-line peak for Pt/WO₂ than that for Pt foil.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier transform Pt L₃-edge EXAFS shows obvious scattering path for Pt-Pt bond at 2.63 Å indicating formation of Pt nanoparticles with Pt⁰ metallic states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform Pt L₃-edge extended X-ray absorption fine-structure (EXAFS) signal for Pt/WO₂ revealed an obvious scattering path corresponding to the Pt-Pt bond at 2.63 Å indicating the formation of Pt nanoparticles with Pt⁰ metallic states.
